Slot Ledger (slot-ledger) is a mixed-integer daily-cost model. Binary truck-leg assignments and cancellations, deadhead links and charge-slot choices enforce coverage and the truck day. For each depot, charger type and slot, the sum of simultaneous charging trucks cannot exceed the available charger count. It therefore represents limited shared capacity, including separate slow and fast pools.

Slot Ledger uses the deterministic 30-minute, whole-wait, lossless constant-power assumptions in EV-S01:P02. It enforces truck and charger power bounds, maintenance exclusion, intermediate battery bounds and final home state of charge at least the initial level. It may optimise cost, but a time-limited feasible solution is not an optimality certificate.

Queue Repair (queue-repair) fixes candidate truck routes for a repair pass, then allocates charging against a per-depot, per-type, per-slot occupancy ledger. A slot is usable only while its count is below the finite charger count. Conflicts move to another valid waiting slot or trigger leg cancellation and route rebuilding; an unresolved conflict is never returned as feasible.

Queue Repair assumes the same known deterministic inputs and 30-minute whole-wait, lossless constant-power charging as EV-S01:P02. It checks coverage, deadheads and return home, truck and charger power, maintenance, battery bounds and final state of charge after repair or cancellation. Fixed candidate routes and repair-or-cancel make this a feasible-plan heuristic, with no claim of global cost optimality.

Slot Ledger Private (private-ledger) gives every truck its own always-available charger. It checks individual energy and charging power but has no depot occupancy sum. It does not model a finite shared charger pool; calling it Slot Ledger without the Private suffix confuses two different formulations.

All methods, authors, experiment results and timings in EV-S01 through EV-S12 are original fiction for this course, not findings attributed to a real paper. P01 supplies a scheduling problem only. There is no uncertain-demand experiment, numerical cost table or evidence of cost superiority in this A/B dossier.

For the tested shared-charger setting with a 60-second solve limit, recommend Queue Repair conditionally on the stated assumptions. Slot Ledger can represent the chargers but the corrected full solve is too slow; Private Ledger is fast but cannot represent their sharing. This is eligibility among the three documented methods, not a claim that Queue Repair is always fastest or cheapest.
